_comment: Guided tour of the micro-time histogram. Targets: names the app remembers (photon_files, detector, ...) and spec attrs/actions (parallel_text, dt_ns, compute). Read by chisurf.emtk.help_guide.

steps.title: From photons to a decay
steps.text: This tool histograms the micro-times of photon files per detector, polarization and excitation window, shows the decay and writes it for the TCSPC analysis. Use Detector definition (the other tab of this dock) for the channels, windows and G-factor of your setup.

steps.title: Generate known demonstration photons
steps.text: Without your own data, generate a clearly synthetic PTU in the settings cache. It contains exactly 3000 VV and 1500 VH photons; the 32 ps header resolution gives a four-channel FWHM of 0.128 ns. The button replaces queued inputs and selects the demonstration setup. It does not start computation or change saved setups.

steps.title: Queue photon files
steps.text: The demonstration file is already queued. For your own measurements, add files, a folder or datasets from the database, or drop them on the window. Untick a file to leave it out; Burst selections (.pto) restrict the photons to bursts.

steps.title: Detector and channels
steps.text: The detector chooses the interleaved routing channels (parallel, perpendicular, ...) and the G-factor; edit the lists by hand when needed.

steps.title: Time step and shifts
steps.text: The time step comes from the file header; shifts pad or clip a histogram to line the VV and VH decays up (they do not wrap photon times).

steps.title: Compute
steps.text: Reads the photons in the background and fills the plot with VV, VH and VV + 2G VH.

steps.title: The decay
steps.text: Cumulative decays of the selected files. The FWHM of the combined trace is shown under the options; Log counts and the trace toggles are above the plot.

steps.title: Save into the container
steps.text: Compute already holds the histogram; Save with Output PTO writes it into the measurement's .pto, where ChiSurf and the provenance view find it. Right-click a photon stream in the PTO Inspector to send it here.
